name: ACCG-2671

lead: ACCG-2671 is an experimental oral amylin agonist being tested for obesity. It is at the very first stage of human testing.
No results have been published, so nothing is known publicly about its effect on weight.

paras: It is described as a small-molecule amylin receptor agonist taken by mouth; amylin agonists are studied for effects on satiety.
Safety and tolerability are the subject of the ongoing first-in-human trial; no data are public. It is not approved.

trials.title: First-in-human Study of the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Food Effect of ACCG-2671

lead: ACCG-2671 is an investigational oral small-molecule amylin receptor agonist being studied for obesity. The only public record of it is a registered first-in-human phase 1/2 trial examining its safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and the effect of food. [1]

No results have been published. Amylin agonists are a class of weight-management candidates that act on satiety pathways, but information specific to this compound is limited to the trial registration.

paras: One trial is registered (NCT07815678), a phase 1/2 first-in-human study of safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and food effect in 164 participants with obesity. It began recruiting in late December 2025. [1] No results have been published.
